paragraphs.text: Nushell as the only shell for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): every shell call runs nu, foreign shells are r
efused before they spawn, and the model is taught Nushell.
# dsh-nu
[](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-nu)
English | 中文
dsh-nu forces DeepSeek Harness to run every shell command in Nushell, with the `bash` / `pwsh` execu
tors disabled. It does three things:
- **Swap the executor**: Through the low-level extension point DeepSeek Harness exposes, it replaces
the `bash` / `pwsh` executor with a Nushell executor at runtime (commands run as `nu --no-config-fi
le -c "<command>"`). dsh still sees the same `bash` / `pwsh` tool with the same calling convention,
so the Nushell executor plugs into dsh and stays compatible with every other plugin and feature. The

oddity is cosmetic: the model calls a tool named `bash` / `pwsh` and passes it Nushell script.
- **
Teach the model**: It adds a short Nushell rules section and syntax guide to the system prompt. That
teaching text costs some context but matters: with it turned off, the model hits frequent errors wh

en calling the shell tool.
- **Refuse handoffs**: When a Nushell command hands work to another shell
, the guard refuses it before a process starts. Bash and PowerShell syntax that Nushell rejects or s
ilently misreads is refused by the syntax rules, with the Nushell spelling in the error.
## Status
0.7.0 is published on npm. dsh `0.2.2-alpha.2` and Nushell `0.116.1` are the tested pair, recorded i
n `package.json` under `testedWith`.
## Compatibility
dsh-nu supports only that pair. The peer ranges cover the dsh family, and boot logs a warning if the
installed dsh or Nushell differs. Other versions have not been tested.
## Install
Requires Node 24.9+, `pnpm` on `PATH` (the `dsh plugin` installer runs it), dsh `0.2.2-alpha.2`, and
Nushell `0.116.1` on `PATH`.
Add the bundle to a dsh profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use `--profile web` for the browser app. The first `dsh plugin` call creates the profile; the bundle
's patch disables the platform shell executors, mounts the Nushell executor and teaching layer, and
re-mounts the shell tool with a Nushell description. Start the profile with `dsh tui` (or `dsh web`)
e-mounts the shell tool with a Nushell description. Start the profile with `dsh tui` (or `dsh web`).
If pnpm reports `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION` for a fresh release, it is applying `minimumRe
leaseAge`. Wait for the cutoff, or add `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0` to the same command.
## Development
The repository ships a flake with the tested Node and Nushell versions:

`dev/link-peers.mjs` links the dsh peer packages into `node_modules`, so the tests can drive the rea
l seams without publishing.
The suite runs on Node 24. The package requires Node 24.9 and newer.
Real-model teaching evals are separate from `npm test`; see `eval/README.md` for the three-arm harne
ss, cross-model judging, and the dated results.
## Nix
dsh-nu does not package dsh itself. This flake builds the plugin from the checkout, and the dsh inst
allation comes from a flake that packages it. The complete example below uses `nur-ryan4yin`, whose
`dsh` also provides the `withPlugins` wrapper that applies bundle patches:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`nix build` produces that `dsh` binary. `mkDshNuPackage` needs only the dsh installation's `@deepsee
k-ai` peer packages, so `llm-agents.nix`'s dsh works there too; applying the bundle still needs a wr
apper that adds `--patch`, which `nur-ryan4yin`'s `withPlugins` provides. Bump the bundle with `nix
flake update dsh-nu`.
## Configuration
The bundle's patch mounts the shell executor, the shell tool row (`nu-tool-bash` on POSIX, `nu-tool-
pwsh` on Windows), and the teaching layer. A profile patch overrides any of them by id. This profile
patch spells out every field and its default:

## What "only Nushell" does not cover
The guard is not a sandbox: it checks command positions it can read, and everything else is out of r
uard is not a sandbox: it checks command positions it can read, and everything else is out of reach.
- A shell name inside a plain quoted string is data, not a command position: `'bash -c "echo hi"'` e
valuates to a string, it does not run bash. `$"…"` and `$'…'` interpolate, so each parenthesized exp

ression inside one is inspected as code; quoted text inside it stays data.
- A literal `nu -c '<scri
pt>'` or `nu -e '<script>'` is inspected recursively, up to four levels. A script value built at run

time is not inspected.
- A Nushell script file is not read: `nu script.nu`, `source`, and `use` loa

d code the guard never sees, so a handoff written into a file and run that way is out of reach.
- A
shell name computed at run time, or a program that starts a shell itself (a language runtime, an edi
tor), is out of reach. The guard follows literal shell names, a fixed launcher table (including `nix

shell` / `nix develop --command` and `nix run`), `run-external`, and literal `nu -c` scripts.
- A t
ool that runs its own argument text is out of scope on purpose: `hyperfine`, `watch`, `make`, `npm r
un`, and `git` hooks are not shell handoffs, so the guard allows them even though they may start `sh
` internally. Refusing them would break the tools rather than keep the deployment Nu-only. When the
command you pass to one of them is Nushell, name the shell: `hyperfine -S nu 'ls | length'`, `hyperf
ine -N 'rg foo'` (no shell at all), or `watch -x rg foo`. Nushell cannot be the shell `watch` starts

by itself, so `watch 'a && b'` runs bash, not Nushell.
- A preset row that spawns its own shell, su
ch as a custom plugin calling `ctx.subprocess.spawn` directly or a PTY persistent-shell group. Disab

le it for a Nu-only deployment; see `examples/preset-nu-shell.md`.
- Other shell seams. Hook bridges
, persistent terminals, and tmux context use their own services or scripts and are outside this bund

le. Keep them off for a strict deployment.
[该节后续省略]
